body:
- **A DTA on carry-forward losses** needs "convincing evidence" of future profit (Ind AS 12). Recognising or reversing it moves PAT without cash.

**Worked example J: Suzlon (SUZLON).**

| | FY24 | FY25 | FY26 |
|---|---|---|---|
| PBT | 659 | 1,447 | 2,422 |
| Tax line | ~0 | **−625 (credit)** | **−741 (credit)** |
| PAT | 660 | 2,072 | 3,163 |
| Effective tax rate (Screener) | −0% | −43% | −31% |

- About ₹1,366 cr of PAT across two years is deferred-tax recognition, not operations.
- On normalised PAT (PBT × ~75%), FY26 is about ₹1,800 cr against 3,163 reported. Any P/E built on 3,163 overstates earnings power by ~75%. *(Amounts derived from Screener's PBT and PAT lines. Confirm the DTA note in the FY26 annual report.)*
- **A DTL growing faster than profits** means tax depreciation is running ahead of book depreciation. That is normal for heavy capex but reverses later.

body:
1. **US filings move the "boring filings" (L13).** There is no BRSR, so headcount comes from the 10-K *human capital* section. The lease note (Topic 842 tables plus "leases committed but not commenced", with dollar totals) gives **rent per new lease** directly: $258M ÷ 141 leases. The **non-GAAP reconciliation in the 8-K Ex-99.1** is where the one-offs hide (the $163.6M tariff refund).
2. **For a widely held US company, the L16 "money to the parent" question becomes "money to management, and what the KPIs leave out".** The useful documents were the 8-K Item 5.02 exhibits (severance, signing bonuses, founder perks, retention awards), the KPI definitions in Items 1 and 7, and Form 4 plus 13G.
3. **Diff the 10-K text year over year.** Deleting "(including beyond $5 per item)" and replacing "by 2030" with "over time" were the cheapest promise-tracker signals in the set.
4. **Triangulate the company's store model against its own capex guidance.** "$100M for ~150 stores" contradicts "$0.4M investment" unless tenant allowances are huge. That made a 2-minute check into the main L3 finding.
5. **Ownership-filing mechanics create false alarms** (the Vanguard realignment) and tool misparses (13F value units). Read the 13G remarks field before reading a 0%.
6. **Two credibility scores:** long-range vs near-term, and by team.
7. **Time spent:** ~70% primary SEC filings (two 10-Ks, 11 8-Ks/exhibits, 80 Form 4s, 13F/13G), ~15% one call transcript (secondary, automated), ~15% estimates. Broker notes were not needed.

**Adjustments that matter:**
- **2024 one-offs.** $56.3M impairment of conventional-frac inventory and a Louisiana tax-law credit. Adjusted EPS was 5.46; the proxy also
  computes 2025 growth on this base (+16%).
- **2025 FCF $406M > NOPAT ~$374M.** Two reasons: (a) deferred tax of $82M; the One Big Beautiful Bill Act restored 100% bonus depreciation,
  and income tax payable fell 100%; (b) capex of $264.5M ≈ D&A of $255M. For a fleet that keeps replacing itself, the cash-tax deferral is
  quasi-permanent. This matters for valuation (§8).
- **SBC is small:** $17.6M, 0.5% of sales, 4% of FCF. Buybacks of $354M (2025) shrank the share count 6%, which is the real owner return
  (no dividend).
- **Segment walk FY2025** `[PR-Q4-25]`:
  - KMT: revenue $1,935.3M, operating income $374.5M (19.3%).
  - KDS: revenue $1,428.7M, operating income $130.8M (9.2%).
  - Corporate: −$13.7M.
- **Quarterly pattern.** Q1 is the weakest quarter (winter delays): Q1-26 operating margin 12.8%, Q2 13.3%, Q3 15.4%. Q4-25 was 15.2%, helped
  by corporate expense of only $0.7M (vs $5–9M in other quarters).
- **Working capital.** Receivables went from $474M (Dec-25) to $711M (Sep-26), with fuel-related billings and power-gen deliveries.
  Inventory was built in late 2025 for 2026 power-gen deliveries `[10K25]`.
